All done. Here's a summary:

**Identified the service:** "payments" wasn't a registered service name — after checking status/deployment tools and confirming with you, the affected service is **payments-worker** (API errors were downstream of the worker).

**Diagnosed:** This morning's deploy of **v3.4.0** was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an **18% error rate**, while **v3.3.0** was the most recent release healthy in production.

**Rolled back:** payments-worker → **v3.3.0** across all production regions. No change-manager approval was needed since v3.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

**Verified recovery:** payments-worker is now healthy again (error rate dropped from 18% → **0.2%**).

**Incident opened:** **INC-0001 (SEV2)** — "payments-worker v3.4.0 causing payment errors — rolled back to v3.3.0", paged to on-call. (The first attempt timed out; I verified no duplicate existed before retrying with the same idempotency key.)

**Remaining follow-up:** Root-cause v3.4.0 before it can be redeployed — deploying it again would require change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.
